question.text: Category I AIFs can borrow funds for temporary requirements for not more than:

answer.text: 90 days, unlimited occasions, 25% of investable funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Category I AIFs cannot borrow for investment purposes, but they may borrow to meet temporary funding and day-to-day requirements for not more than 30 days, on not more than four occasions in a year, and not more than 10% of investable funds. A 30-day cooling-off period must be maintained between two such borrowing transactions. Similar limits apply to Category II AIFs. The Trap: Option B is the keyed answer and matches the SEBI restriction. The other options inflate the day-count, occasion-count, or percentage caps and are not permitted under the workbook. Note: Edits remove the earlier pro-tip claim that investor capital is not exposed to leveraged losses. The workbook only supports that Category I/II borrowing is tightly restricted to temporary funding/day-to-day requirements; it does not endorse a broader risk-comparison statement.
